events.summary: VIAVI announced that its Aerospace and Defense business achieved CMMC Level 2 certification, a mandatory US Department of Defense cybersecurity standard for contractors handling controlled unclassified information. It covers its radio test, avionics, synthetic and modular, and Position, Navigation and Timing product lines. The stock rose 9.27% on 2026-09-25 (pipeline). Investing.com credited the certification plus a 2026-09-23 analyst note (Rosenblatt reiterated Buy, $70 target).
events.why_it_matters: Without this certification, VIAVI could not keep selling to many US defense customers, so it protects existing sales. Aerospace and defense is about 17% of NSE revenue. It is a permission to sell, not a new contract.

products.name: VIAVI company overview (two segments)
products.what_it_is: VIAVI makes test-and-measurement equipment and software for networks (NSE segment, ~80% of revenue) and specialty optical coatings and filters (OSP segment, ~20%).
products.analogy: NSE is like the diagnostic machines a car mechanic plugs in, but for internet links, data centers and radios. OSP is like a maker of special inks and lenses, such as the color-shifting ink on banknotes.
products.buyers: Data-center chip, optics and equipment makers and hyperscalers' suppliers; telecom/cable operators; aerospace and defense; for OSP, central-bank currency printers and consumer-electronics makers (OSP buyer detail from general knowledge of the 10-K; not re-verified this run).
products.how_it_works: NSE sells hardware testers plus software that send traffic through a link or device and measure errors, speed and security. Spirent (acquired) adds Ethernet/AI-network and security testing. OSP sells thin-film optical pigments and filters.
products.competition: Keysight Technologies is the main test-and-measurement rival (general knowledge, not sourced this run)
products.why_investors_care: NSE has become an AI data-center story; OSP is a steady, high-margin cash business (40% Q4 operating margin per call highlights).
products.watch_next: Q1 FY27 results (estimated 2026-10-28): revenue vs $450-460M guidance and margin vs 27.1%.

products.name: Data-center ecosystem test portfolio (high-speed Ethernet / 1.6T, PCIe 7.0, Ultra Ethernet validation, Spirent products)
products.what_it_is: Testers that check whether the very fast connections inside AI data centers (800G/1.6T optical links, PCIe chip-to-chip links, Ultra Ethernet AI networking) work correctly before they ship.
products.analogy: A crash-test lab for data highways: before a new car (network chip or optical module) goes on sale, you run it hard on a test track and record every failure.
products.buyers: Makers of network chips, optical transceivers, switches and servers, and the labs of large cloud companies (category; named customers not disclosed)
products.how_it_works: The tester generates huge streams of traffic at line rate, sends them through the device or link, and measures bit errors, latency and protocol compliance. It is used both in R&D labs and on factory lines.
products.sales: not disclosed as a separate number. Proxy: management said the data-center ecosystem is ~50% of NSE revenue and 'more than doubled' year over year excluding Spirent. 50% of Q4 NSE $353.9M implies roughly $177M for the quarter (labelled inference from rounded % ).
products.stage: shipping and ramping. Ultra Ethernet validation launched 2026-06-23; showcased at ECOC 2026 (VIAVI release 2026-09-09).
products.size_for_company: About 40% of total quarterly revenue (inference: ~50% of NSE, and NSE is 79.9% of revenue)
products.competition: Keysight and others in high-speed network test (not sourced this run)
products.why_investors_care: This is the AI exposure behind the stock's +164% year-to-date run, and the reason it trades with optical stocks.
products.watch_next: Whether data-center share and NSE growth hold in Q1 FY27. Management target: $500M quarterly revenue during calendar 2027.

products.name: CyberFlood CF50 (100G application, security and AI-inference test platform)
products.what_it_is: A small 100G test box that simulates real application and attack traffic to test firewalls, security gear and AI-inference systems (announced 2026-09-29).
products.analogy: A sparring partner that throws realistic punches (traffic and cyberattacks) at a security guard (firewall) to see whether it holds up.
products.buyers: Enterprise security vendors, network-equipment makers, enterprises (category; customers not disclosed)
products.how_it_works: Generates stateful application traffic and attack scenarios at up to 100G and measures throughput and blocking.
products.size_for_company: not disclosed; likely small relative to $443M quarterly revenue (inference, low)
products.why_investors_care: Shows Spirent's security-test line being refreshed. A minor item.
products.watch_next: Any order or customer mentions on the Q1 FY27 call.

guidance.longer_term: $500M quarterly revenue achievable during calendar 2027 (management, per call highlights)
